title: The Evening Brief: FIFA opposition hardens as deadline deals reshape rosters
dek: England's formal withdrawal of support for Gianni Infantino joined UEFA's legal threat and a document preservation letter as the FIFA governance crisis deepened, while MLB and WNBA trade deadlines produced a wave of roster moves across both leagues.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: FIFA's governance crisis escalated from institutional opposition to a formal legal threat, while the day's trade deadlines were dominated by teams pursuing pitching and win-now deals rather than long rebuilds.
bottom_line: FIFA's crisis moved from institutional opposition to a formal legal footing, with UEFA's document preservation letter to Infantino and to private parties including Joshua Kushner, Greg Maffei, and JP Morgan following Thursday's boycott vote and England's and Wales's withdrawal of support. MLB and WNBA trade deadlines reshaped several rosters, with the Rays, Cubs, and Guardians adding pitching and the Sparks trading Kelsey Plum to the Mercury in the fourth midseason All-Star deal in league history. The reporting ties the FIFA opposition to the scrapped private equity plan and does not go further; the trade moves are documented by terms and current form, not by outcome. The coming days will show whether further confederations withdraw support, whether UEFA's legal threat becomes a filed action, and how the newly traded players perform for their new teams.
body: The day's central story remained FIFA. UEFA has raised the possibility of legal action against Infantino over his now-scrapped plan to create a $20 billion private entity to run the World Cup, and sent Infantino a document preservation letter, a formal demand to retain all documents tied to the proposal. UEFA also wrote to private parties involved in the plan, including Joshua Kushner, Greg Maffei, and JP Morgan, signaling the confederation is building toward possible litigation. That escalation followed UEFA's 55 member nations voting on Thursday to boycott the World Cup and all other FIFA competitions in protest, a vote that predates both Infantino's Friday reversal of the plan and this weekend's document preservation letter.

Institutional opposition widened alongside the legal threat. Wales became the first nation to publicly withdraw support for Infantino's leadership, and England's FA is now set to write to FIFA doing the same, according to ESPN and BBC Sport reporting. Both federations had previously submitted letters backing Infantino's reelection at next year's Congress; both reversed course after his private equity proposal drew opposition from UEFA, Concacaf, and the AFC. Infantino will need 106 votes from FIFA's 211 member nations to win a fourth term at the March 2027 Congress, a threshold that the reporting describes as still mathematically intact even as the political ground shifts.

Away from FIFA, the day was dominated by trade activity. MLB's deadline produced a run of pitching moves: the Rays acquired Freddy Peralta from the Mets, sending three prospects to New York; the Cubs acquired Kevin Gausman from the Blue Jays while sitting 6.5 games behind the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Central; and the Guardians made two separate additions, acquiring All-Star left-hander Foster Griffin from the Nationals and outfielder Jo Adell from the Angels for catching prospect Jacob Cozart. Adell posted a strong 2025 (.778 OPS, 37 home runs) but has slumped to .239/.287/.395 in 2026, a step down from the .211/.268/.381 mark and minus-7 WAR he posted across 308 games from 2020 to 2024; he is not eligible for free agency until after the 2027 season concludes, giving Cleveland multi-year control.

The WNBA's deadline centered on Kelsey Plum, traded from the Sparks to the Mercury for Monique Akoa Makani, a 2027 first-round pick, and a 2028 second-round pick, only the fourth midseason All-Star trade in league history. Plum has been out since June 21 with a lower left leg injury and her timeline in Phoenix is unclear. The Sparks, at 10-17 with a six-game losing streak, framed the move as a formal reset after a contention push that did not stabilize the roster.

Elsewhere, Marc Skinner departed Manchester United Women by mutual consent after five years, with one year left on a contract he had renewed in 2024. Victory+ removed CEO Neil Gruninger after losing the Rangers, NWSL, and Ducks rights deals within two weeks, replacing him with Jon Spencer of TriWest Capital Partners; the platform's remaining partners, including the Dallas Stars and Minnesota Lynx, were reported secure. Alex Eala won her first WTA title at the DC Open, beating Jessica Pegula in three sets to become the first Filipina to win a WTA 500 event. Shiho Kuwaki won the Women's Open at Royal Lytham & St Annes after Esther Henseleit's playoff drive struck a course marshal. Notre Dame and USC agreed to resume their rivalry in 2030, with both Week 1 games set. Olivia Miles scored 28 points in a Lynx win over the Fever but drew her third technical foul of the season. Bryan Bresee will miss the Saints' season after tearing his ACL in a noncontact training camp injury. And USA cricketer Bodugum Akhilesh Reddy was banned eight years by the ICC for match-fixing in the 2025 Abu Dhabi T10 League.

The reporting attributes the FIFA opposition directly to the scrapped private equity plan, and attributes the trade deadline activity to teams positioning rosters ahead of stretch runs, but does not offer further causal detail beyond what is stated. The Victory+ leadership change is tied explicitly to the lost rights deals; the reporting does not say whether other factors contributed.

What to watch: whether other confederations follow England and Wales in formally withdrawing support, and whether UEFA's document preservation letter develops into a filed legal action. On the trade front, whether Peralta, Gausman, Griffin, and Adell perform differently in new uniforms, and whether Plum's leg injury clears in time to affect Phoenix's playoff push. Skinner's successor at Manchester United, Victory+'s next moves under Jon Spencer, and Bresee's recovery timeline in New Orleans round out the near-term checkpoints.
